body_ar:
الكلام على فتح بيت المقدس قبل المسيح عليه السلام

هل سيفتح بيت المقدس قبل المسيح عيسى بن مريم؟

نعم سيفتح بيت المقدس ويحرر في الحرب الأولى على اليهود، فيحاربهم المسلمون فيكون اليهود غربي نهر الأردن والمسلمون شرقيه فتفتح القدس يفتحها المسلمون وتسقط دولة اليهود ويتفرقون في الأرض ثم بعد ذلك يخرج الدجال، فيجتمع عليه فلول اليهود، وبعد ذلك بثماني سنوات أقصد بعد فتح بيت المقدس بثماني سنوات يخرج الدجال، فبعد فتح بيت المقدس مباشرة تفتح روما وبعد فتح روما في الثامنة أي في السنة الثامنة يخرج الدجال، وإذا خرج الدجال فسينزل عيسى ابن مريم بعد خروج الدجال، وبذلك يعلم أن فتح روما وفتح بيت المقدس كلاهما قبل نزول المسيح بن مريم عليه السلام.

----------------------------------------------------------------------

النبي و المرسل

هل جاء في القرآن أسماء أنبياء غير مرسلين؟

اختلف أهل العلم في الفرق بين النبي و الرسول إلى أقوال كثيرة و لم يرد في ذلك نص عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم و المرجع في ذلك إلى اللغة فالنبي فعيل إما أن تكون بمعنى مفعل2 أو أن تكون بمعنى مفعل3 فإذا كانت بمعنى مفعل (بفتح العين) فإما أن تكون من النبإ الذي هو الخبر أو من النبوة التي هي الارتفاع فإذا كان النبيء فعيلا بمعنى المفعول من النبإ معناه أنه منبأ عن الله أي يأتيه النبأ و هو الخبر من عند الله و إذا كان بمعنى الفاعل فمعناه أنه منبأ أي أنه مخبر عن الله و إذا كانت من النبوة و هي الارتفاع فمعناه أن الله قد رفع منزلته فكل من رفع الله منزلته من عباده إلى هذا المقام بحيث يأتيه النبأ من عند الله فهو نبي

و قد اختلف هل يمكن أن يتصف بذلك النساء و نحوهن و الراجح جواز ذلك لأن الوحي قد جاء نزوله إلى بعض النساء في القرآن فجاء الوحي إلى أم موسى و كذلك فإن مريم عليها السلام خاطبها الله تعالى و جاءها الملك فكلمها و هذا يقتضي الوحي و لذلك قال السيوطي رحمه الله: اختلفت في خضر أهل النقــول لقمان ذي القرنين حوا مريم قيــل نبي أو ولي أو رســـــــــول و الوقف في الجميع رأي المعظم

لكن الأدلة قائمة على أن النبوة حاصلة ثم الرسالة هي أن يؤمر بتبليغ ذلك لأنه واضح جدا من لفظ الرسول أنه مأمور بالبلاغ لأن الرسول في اللغة يطلق على أمرين يطلق على الرسالة نفسها فهي رسول في اللغة و من ذلك قول الشاعر: لقد كذب الواشون ما بحت عندهم بليلى و ما أرسلتهم برسول ما أرسلتهم برسول:أي ما أرسلتهم برسالة.

ثم يطلق الرسول أيضا على الفعول للمبالغة من الرسالة أي الذي يخرج من مكان إلى آخر لا يخرجه إلا هذه الرسالة فأنت إذا أرسلت شخصا من هنا إلى مكان معين يحمل أمانة ليؤديها فهو رسول أما إذا وجدت مسافرا إلى ذلك المكان فأرسلت معه تلك الأمانة فهذا ليس رسولا لأنك لم تكلفه بها بل قد سافر هو لحاجته و أنت ائتمنته على هذه الأمانة فإذن هذا الفرق و لذلك جيء بمفعول للمبالغة لأن حامل الرسالة إذا لم تكن له مهمة إلا إبلاغ الرسالة فهو رسول و إلا كان مؤتمنا عليها من غير أن يكون رسولا

و على هذا فإن الذين ذكروا في القرآن من أنبياء الله و الذين سموا و هم ثمانية عشرفي سورة الأنعام و بقيتهم يكمل بها خمسة و عشرون و قد ذكر أكثرهم في آية النساء و في آية الأنعام وجميعهم خمسة و عشرون هؤلاء جميعا أنبياء و رسل على الراجح و قد جاء ذكر الأسباط بصيغة الجمع و لم يرد تسميتهم فرادى فجاء ذكرهم في مجال الوحي و هو ما أنزله الله فقد قال الله تعالى: (قولوا آمنا بالله و ما أنزل إلينا و ما أنزل إلى إبراهيم و إسماعيل و إسحاق و يعقوب و الأسباط و ما أوتي موسى و عيسى و ما أوتي النبيون من ربهم) فهنا بين أن الأسباط أنزل إليهم و هذا يقتضي أنهم أنبياء و رسل لكن لم يسموا فعلى هذا كل من ذكر في القرآن من الأنبياء فهو رسول نبي و من سوى ذلك منهم الأنبياء و منهم الرسل.

----------------------------------------------------------------------

النية المطلوبة عند الصدقة

هل يمكنني إذا مرضت أو مرض لي شخص أن أتصدق بنية دفع الضرر؟

أن الصدقة ترفع البلاء وتزيد في العمر، لكن ينبغي أن تكون النية فيها خالصة لوجه الله، أن يقصد الشخص بها التقرب إلى الله، ومع ذلك فستكون هي سببا لرفع البلاء وشفاء المرضى، ولكن لا ينبغي أن يشترط الشخص ذلك على الله في حال تصدقه، بل ينبغي أن يتصدق مخلصا لله فقط عند أي بلاء أو عند أي صباح أو أي مساء، فكل ذلك وقت للصدقة التي يرفع الله بها البلاء ويزيد بها في العمر.

----------------------------------------------------------------------

الوساوس في العقيدة

امرأة ابتلاها الله بالوساوس والشكوك منذ زمن طويل ويصل بها ذلك في بعض الأحيان إلى الشك في بعض جزئيات العقيدة فما هو العلاج لحالتها هذه؟

إن هذه الحالة هي من عمل الشيطان وعليها إذا وجدت شيئا من ذلك أن تقول«ءامنت بالله» وأن تكثر من ذكر الله والاستغفار فإن الشيطان سرعان ما يخنس إذا ذكر الله سبحانه وتعالى

فإذا وسوس الشيطان إلى الإنسان في جانب العقيدة فليبادر إلى الإستغفار وإلى ذكر الله تعالى و ليكثر من الذكر بما تيسر له فإن ذلك يطرد عنه الشيطان ويمنعه

وقد صح في صحيح مسلم من حديث عثمان ابن أبي العاص الثقفي رضي الله عنه قال أتيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقلت يا رسول الله إن الشيطان كاد يفتنني عن صلاتي وقراءتي فقال: «ذلك شيطان اسمه خنزب إذا وجدت ذلك فانفث عن يسارك ثلاثا وقل أعوذ بالله من خنزب»

فعلى المؤمن أن يستعيذ بالله من الشيطان دائما وأن يعلم أن الوسواس هو من عمله وأن الله سبحانه وتعالى ينهاه عن إتباع خطوات الشيطان وهذا من إتباعها فعليه أن لا يلقي الزمام للشيطان بل يبرأ إلى الله منه ويكثر من الإستغفار وسرعان ما يذهب عنه ذلك الوسواس

ثم عليه كذلك أن يتصل بأهل الإيمان وأهل القوة في الله فإن الشيطان لا يقوى عليهم من كان يجالس أهل الإيمان والقوة في الله سبحانه وتعالى و أهل القرءان فإن الشيطان لا يقوى عليه بحال من الأحوال و يفر منه وكذلك الذي يصلي الفرائض الخمس في المسجد دائما لا يكون من أهل الوسواس في الغالب و كذلك الذي يحافظ على الطهارة و يستتر من البول لا يكون من أهل الوسواس في الغالب فهذه الأمور دفع و وقاية من الوسواس.
body_en:
On the conquest of Jerusalem before the Messiah, peace be upon him

Will Jerusalem be conquered before the Messiah Jesus son of Mary?

Yes, Jerusalem will be conquered and liberated in the first war against the Jews. The Muslims will fight them, and the Jews will be west of the River Jordan and the Muslims east of it, and Jerusalem will be conquered — the Muslims will conquer it — and the state of the Jews will fall and they will be scattered through the earth. Then after that the Dajjal will come forth, and the remnants of the Jews will gather to him. And eight years after that — I mean eight years after the conquest of Jerusalem — the Dajjal will come forth; for immediately after the conquest of Jerusalem, Rome will be conquered, and after the conquest of Rome, in the eighth — that is, in the eighth year — the Dajjal will come forth. And when the Dajjal comes forth, Jesus son of Mary will descend after the coming forth of the Dajjal. By this it is known that the conquest of Rome and the conquest of Jerusalem are both before the descent of the Messiah son of Mary, peace be upon him.

----------------------------------------------------------------------

The prophet and the one sent as messenger

Do the names of prophets who were not sent as messengers occur in the Qur'an?

The scholars differed over the difference between the prophet (nabī) and the messenger (rasūl), into many positions, and no explicit text (naṣṣ) on it has come from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The reference in this is to the language. The word nabī is of the pattern faʿīl: it is either in the sense of mufʿal or in the sense of mufʿil. If it is in the sense of mufʿal (with a fatḥah on the ʿayn), then it is either from al-nabaʾ, which is news, or from al-nubuwwah, which is elevation. So if nabīʾ is faʿīl in the sense of the passive participle, from al-nabaʾ, its meaning is that he is one informed from God — that is, the news, the report, comes to him from God. And if it is in the sense of the active participle, its meaning is that he is one who gives news, that is, one who informs from God. And if it is from al-nubuwwah, which is elevation, its meaning is that God has raised his station. So everyone of His servants whose station God has raised to this rank, such that the news comes to him from God, is a prophet.

They differed as to whether women and the like can be so described. The stronger view is that this is possible, because the descent of revelation to some women has occurred in the Qur'an: revelation came to the mother of Moses; and likewise Mary, peace be upon her, was addressed by God, exalted, and the angel came to her and spoke with her, and this entails revelation. That is why al-Suyuti, may God have mercy on him, said: *The transmitters differed over Khidr — it was said: a prophet, or a friend of God, or a messenger; and over Luqman, Dhu al-Qarnayn, Eve and Mary — and suspending judgement on all of them is the view of most.*

But the evidences stand that prophethood is realised. Then messengerhood is that one is commanded to convey it, because it is very clear from the word rasūl that he is commanded to convey. For rasūl in the language is applied to two things. It is applied to the message itself — a message is a rasūl in the language — and of that is the poet's saying: *The slanderers lied; I disclosed nothing about Layla in their presence, and I did not send them with a message.* 'And I did not send them with a rasūl' means: and I did not send them with a message.

Then rasūl is also applied to the intensive pattern faʿūl from 'message', that is, one who goes out from one place to another with nothing taking him out but this message. So if you send someone from here to a particular place carrying a trust to deliver, he is a messenger; whereas if you find someone travelling to that place and send that trust with him, he is not a messenger, because you did not charge him with it — rather he travelled for his own need and you entrusted him with this trust. So this is the difference; and for that reason the intensive pattern was used, because if the bearer of the message has no task but conveying the message, he is a messenger, and otherwise he is one entrusted with it without being a messenger.

On this basis, those of God's prophets who are mentioned in the Qur'an and are named — and they are eighteen in Sūrat al-Anʿām, and the rest complete twenty-five with them; most of them are mentioned in the verse of al-Nisāʾ and in the verse of al-Anʿām, and altogether they are twenty-five — all of these are prophets and messengers, on the stronger view. The tribes (al-asbāṭ) are mentioned in the plural form and are not named individually; they are mentioned in the context of revelation, which is what God sent down. God, exalted, said: {Say: we believe in God, and in what was sent down to us, and what was sent down to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob and the tribes, and what was given to Moses and Jesus, and what was given to the prophets from their Lord} (Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:136). Here He made clear that it was sent down to the tribes, and this entails that they are prophets and messengers, but they were not named. On this basis, everyone mentioned in the Qur'an among the prophets is a messenger-prophet; and as for those besides them, among them are prophets and among them are messengers.

----------------------------------------------------------------------

The intention required when giving charity

If I fall ill, or someone belonging to me falls ill, may I give charity with the intention of warding off harm?

Voluntary charity (ṣadaqah) lifts affliction and increases the life span; but the intention in it should be purely for the face of God, so that the person intends by it drawing near to God. Even so, it will be a cause for the lifting of affliction and the healing of the sick. But the person should not make that a stipulation upon God at the time of his giving; rather he should give charity sincerely for God alone — at any affliction, or at any morning, or any evening. All of that is a time for the charity by which God lifts affliction and by which He increases the life span.

----------------------------------------------------------------------

Obsessive whisperings concerning creed

A woman whom God has tried with obsessive whisperings and doubts for a long time, which sometimes brings her to doubt some particulars of creed — what is the remedy for this condition of hers?

This condition is from the work of Satan. When she finds anything of that, she should say 'I believe in God', and should make much remembrance of God and seeking of forgiveness, for Satan quickly withdraws when God, glorified and exalted, is remembered.

So if Satan whispers to a person in the matter of creed, let him hasten to seek forgiveness and to remember God, exalted, and let him make much remembrance, with whatever is easy for him, for that drives Satan away from him and holds him off.

It is soundly established in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, from the hadith of Uthman ibn Abi al-As al-Thaqafi, may God be pleased with him, who said: I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said, 'O Messenger of God, Satan has all but come between me and my prayer and my recitation.' He said: 'That is a devil called Khinzib. When you find that, spit dryly to your left three times and say: I seek refuge in God from Khinzib.'

So the believer must always seek refuge in God from Satan, and must know that obsessive whispering is from his work, and that God, glorified and exalted, forbids him to follow the footsteps of Satan — and this is one of the ways of following them. So he must not hand the reins to Satan; rather let him disown him before God and make much seeking of forgiveness, and that obsessive whispering will soon leave him.

Then he must also keep contact with the people of faith and the people of strength in God, for Satan has no power over them. Whoever sits with the people of faith and of strength in God, glorified and exalted, and with the people of the Qur'an — Satan has no power over him in any circumstance whatever, and flees from him. Likewise, one who always prays the five obligatory prayers in the mosque is usually not among the people of obsessive whispering; and likewise one who keeps to ritual purity and shields himself from urine is usually not among the people of obsessive whispering. These things repel obsessive whispering and guard against it.

flags.note: EDITORIAL REVIEW REQUIRED (style guide §12). The first item is an end-times sequence stated as fact, involving a war against the Jews, the fall of 'the state of the Jews', and a dated eight-year interval. It has been translated exactly as given, neither softened nor sharpened, and nothing has been added. In English, detached from the eschatological genre it belongs to, it will be read as political prediction, with obvious consequences in several jurisdictions. Note also that the Sheikh cites no hadith and no source anywhere in this item, and no citation has been supplied. The decision whether and how to publish belongs to Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office.

flags.arabic: اختلفت في خضر أهل النقــول / لقمان ذي القرنين حوا مريم / قيــل نبي أو ولي أو رســـــــــول / و الوقف في الجميع رأي المعظم
flags.context: al-Suyuti's two lines of verse as printed on the page
options: read as two lines whose hemistichs the page has printed out of order, and translate by meaning (as done here)
translate the four half-lines in the printed order
leave the verse untranslated and carry only the Sheikh's framing
flags.note: SOURCE / EXTRACTION DEFECT. The four half-lines rhyme as النقول/رسول and مريم/المعظم, which means the page has printed the two first hemistichs, then the two second hemistichs — the flattening of a two-column layout. Read in the printed order the verse is not intelligible. The English restores the pairing by sense; body_ar preserves the printed order untouched. A reviewer with al-Suyuti's text should confirm.

flags.arabic: إما أن تكون بمعنى مفعل2 أو أن تكون بمعنى مفعل3
flags.context: فالنبي فعيل إما أن تكون بمعنى مفعل2 أو أن تكون بمعنى مفعل3 فإذا كانت بمعنى مفعل (بفتح العين)
options: read the stray digits as lost vowel marks distinguishing mufʿal from mufʿil, and translate accordingly
reproduce the digits in the English as printed
mark the two words as illegible in the source
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT. The page prints مفعل2 and مفعل3 — the same consonantal skeleton twice, with stray digits where vowel marks or footnote markers were lost in the CMS. The Sheikh's own next clause, 'if it is in the sense of mufʿal (with a fatḥah on the ʿayn)', and the passive/active explanation that follows, show that the pair intended is mufʿal (passive) and mufʿil (active). The English uses that reading; the digits are preserved in body_ar and have not been carried into the English.

flags.arabic: و قد اختلف هل يمكن أن يتصف بذلك النساء و نحوهن و الراجح جواز ذلك
flags.context: the Sheikh's position that women may be described as prophets
options: the stronger view is that this is possible
the preponderant view is that it is permissible
the sounder opinion is that it may be so
flags.note: الراجح جواز ذلك here concerns whether the description can validly apply, not a legal permission, so 'permissible' in the five-rulings sense must be avoided. This is a live and contested question in the tradition, and the Sheikh states his own position briefly and without qualification; it has not been hedged.

translator_notes: Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.

Four separate fatwas are published on this one page, divided in the source by rules of hyphens. The rules are preserved in both body_ar and body_en so the boundaries survive; the site should render them as four separate items. Each item's own heading is part of the source text and has been kept.

In the second item the Qur'anic quotation is given in the source inside ordinary round brackets and without a reference. The English uses the house braces and supplies the reference (Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:136); the Arabic has not been altered.
The lines of verse (al-Suyuti, and the anonymous line on Layla) are rendered as prose in italics per house style; the Arabic should be displayed alongside. The Sheikh names no poet for the second.
The grading in the fourth item is the Sheikh's own: soundly established in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, from Uthman ibn Abi al-As. It has been carried exactly.

Source spellings preserved verbatim in body_ar: ثمانية عشرفي written without a space, الإستغفار and إتباع with connecting hamzas, ءامنت and القرءان written with the alif-madda split, and المسيح بن مريم without the alif of ابن; and 'برسالة.ثم', where the source runs two sentences together with no space after the full stop. body_ar reproduces every one of these; the only whitespace the translation introduces is the paragraph breaks that mirror the English paragraphing.
dec: An end-times sequence stated as fact, involving a war against the Jews and the fall of ‘the state of the Jews’, with a dated interval and no source given.
